findings.summary: The chapter says global CSS may be imported only in the root layout, but the App Router allows it in any layout, page or component.
findings.evidence: "import './globals.css' only in root app/layout.tsx" (page 1) and "Global CSS | resets, variables; root layout only" (page 6)
findings.fix: Reword to say global CSS can be imported from any layout, page or component under app/, but by convention and for predictable ordering it is imported once in the root layout.

findings.summary: Code is shown before the idea behind it is stated and the example is not introduced by a one-line idea.
findings.evidence:
Combine classes with a template string or clsx
tsx
import styles from './x.module.css'
findings.fix: Place a one-line idea above the snippet, such as 'Import the module as styles, then use styles.name as the className', and show a clsx example if clsx is mentioned.

findings.summary: The Modules vs Global table has an empty header cell, and its closing line repeats the table in a prose sentence.
findings.evidence: Site-wide and order-dependent: use Modules for component styles.
findings.fix: Label the first column 'Aspect' and make the closing line a short callout that says only 'Use Modules for component styles; keep Global minimal'.

findings.summary: A bullet holds two ideas: the :global escape hatch and the rule that bare selectors are not allowed.
findings.evidence: Bare h1 {} is not allowed: pair it with a class or use :global(h1)
findings.fix: Split it into two bullets: 'Bare element selectors are not allowed', and 'Pair the element with a class, or wrap it in :global(h1)'.

findings.summary: Several bullets hold more than one idea, and the install commands and config are listed before the idea is stated.
findings.evidence: v4 loads with one line in globals.css: @import "tailwindcss"; / No tailwind.config.js or three @tailwind directives by default
findings.fix: Give each bullet one idea (what the one-line import does; that v4 needs no config file or @tailwind directives), and state the idea before each code block.

findings.summary: One bullet packs a token rule, its naming effect and its example together, and the 'Plain CSS' bullet is a separate idea inside the same list.
findings.evidence: @theme in CSS adds tokens; --color-brand gives bg-brand and text-brand
findings.fix: Split into 'Add tokens with @theme' and '--color-brand generates bg-brand and text-brand'.

findings.summary: The 'Interview Point' section asks questions with answers inline and repeats them verbatim on the cheat sheet, and the '1. Why Runtime CSS-in-JS Breaks' bullets use a colon to chain two ideas.
findings.evidence: Import one there: fails at build or render
findings.fix: Split the chained bullets, and keep the interview Q&A on one page only, or format it as a question/answer table.

findings.summary: The state-sharing bullets mix several ideas (lift state, Context, where the provider lives, how Server Components pass through), so the sharing flow is hard to skim.
findings.fix: Show the flow as a small diagram: Provider (Client, layout.tsx) → {children} (Server Components) → consumers, and keep one idea per bullet.

findings.summary: The Reading and Writing Params section mixes server and client code, with bullet explanations placed after the snippets and several unrelated rules stacked at the end.
findings.evidence:
searchParams is a Promise; using it makes the route dynamic
push adds a history entry; replace does not
useSearchParams without Suspense can bail out static rendering of the page
findings.fix: State each idea before its snippet, and split the stacked bullets into one rule each, or use a Server vs Client table.

findings.summary: The theme-flash diagram is a list of fragments, and the rules beneath it hold more than one idea per bullet.
findings.evidence: Colours as CSS variables per theme; toggle only the attribute
findings.fix: Number the steps with arrows, and split into 'Define colours as CSS variables per theme' and 'Toggle only the attribute'.

findings.summary: The cheat sheet repeats the theme fix and the interview Q&A from earlier pages, and the term 'Blocking inline script' is introduced as a script elsewhere, so the same fix is described in different words.
findings.evidence:
Blocking inline script in <head>, or a cookie
suppressHydrationWarning on <html>
findings.fix: Use one term (for example 'blocking inline script in <head>') on pages 5, 6 and 7, and trim duplicated interview questions.

findings.summary: The cheat sheet says useSearchParams 'needs' a Suspense boundary, while page 5 says it 'can bail out static rendering' without one, which are different claims.
findings.fix: Align wording: 'useSearchParams without Suspense can bail out static rendering; wrap it in Suspense'.
